subject: biology-2
question: Some researchers once argued that life could not arise from nonliving matter and must have been carried to Earth from elsewhere in space. Which evidence best supports **abiogenesis**, the origin of life from nonliving chemicals, instead?

options.text: Meteorites that contain living bacterial cells have been recovered and grown in the laboratory.
Miller-Urey style experiments produce organic building blocks from simple gases under early Earth conditions.
All modern cells arise only from preexisting cells, so the same must have been true in the past.
Organic molecules have never been found outside a living organism.

explanation: Abiogenesis holds that life arose from nonliving chemistry, and Miller-Urey style experiments show organic building blocks forming from simple gases under early Earth conditions, exactly the first step such a process would need. A is unsupported, since no living cells have ever been recovered from meteorites. C describes biogenesis, which governs how existing life reproduces, not how life began. D is false, because organic molecules form naturally in many places with no organism present.
